The building control body should be provided with a report that demonstrates that the residential building passes CIBSEs TM59 assessment of overheating.
The heat loss from the floor should be calculated using the sum of the thermal resistance of the floor finish and the underlying heated layer, multiplied by 10.
The net heating energy demand for ventilation shall be calculated on the basis of the heating of air after heat recovery to supply air temperature and any heating before heat recovery.
For space heating systems, temperature control should be installed for the heating appliance.
The water meter of a property shall be located in a place where it is easy to install, read and service and where it cannot freeze.
Air pressure tests should be performed following the guidance in the approved airtightness testing methodology, CIBSEs TM23.
A handrail and its ending must be shaped safely and must continue past the start and end points of the structure.
Where controls are integrated in the heater, the system should be provided with a time switch/programmer and room temperature sensor linked to heater firing and fan speed control.
Where the dwelling is defined as wheelchair adaptable, it should be easy to install a lift.

Dwellings, accommodation premises, institutions, day-care institutions, day-care centres and other early childhood education premises and schools must be provided with an appropriate system that gives a warning at an early stage of a beginning fire.
People should be able to see other people approaching from the opposite direction, thereby allowing sufficient reaction time for both parties to avoid a collision.
No individual flight has a rise between landings of more than 1800mm.
The index terminal flow rate should be set with the terminal fully open and all other terminals should be adjusted to achieve the required flow rates at each terminal.
Windows, glass walls and glass doors into which there is a danger of collision must be marked in such a way that they can be easily noticed.
In the case of the storey-level door of a dwelling, or if the number of people evacuating through the door exceeds 60, doors must open in the direction of the exit.
If the circulation piping is located inside the building envelope, 50 of the calculated domestic hot water circulation heat loss shall be added to the thermal load of the spaces of the building.
For rooflights, U-values should be calculated based on a horizontal position.
Any justification and strategy should be in line with the approved airtightness testing methodology, CIBSEs TM23.
The annual percentage of heat supplied from each heat source should be the same for each newly connected dwelling.

If other performance (e.g. wind load, safety, security or acoustic attenuation) requires thicker glass to be used, an equivalent window unit with standard thickness glazing should be shown to meet the required standard.
The building fabric should be constructed so that thermal bridging, including at the party wall, is reasonably limited.
If a new building has a space heating or airconditioning system with an effective rated output greater than 180kW, a building automation and control system should be installed.
The use of recirculation, transfer or secondary air shall not cause any harmful spread of impurities, in particular odours.
To correctly assess whether an element meets the limiting U-value, the U-value must be calculated for the element in the appropriate plane - either horizontal or vertical.
Door rails, stiles and muntins should be at least 44mm thick.
Where a lift is provided, it should be suitable for a wheelchair user.

The building emission rate and building primary energy rate submission should be accompanied by a report, signed by a suitably qualified person, detailing how the combined emission factor has been derived.
Every single bedroom has a minimum floor area of 8.5m2 and is at least 2.4m wide.
The selection of relevant critical situations for design should be made reflecting the conditions that can reasonably be foreseen during future use.
A building with a height exceeding 9 metres must be equipped with anchoring structures for safety lines.
Ramps, steps, thresholds and differences in levels in passageways must be clearly indicated using lighting and surface brightness contrasts or warning signs.

In order to enhance the efficiency of firefighting and rescue operations, means of smoke extraction shall be designed and constructed in the building so that smoke can be extracted from the different premises in the building.
The number of appliances should not exceed one per 100m2 of dwelling floor area.
A driveway must not intersect a walkway leading to a play area.
For large roofs, where the smaller horizontal dimension of the roof is 50 m or more, and the topography is windswept, the value of the exposure coefficient shall be at least 1.

The structure of the exterior wall against the ground must be waterproofed or isolated against water pressure or a structurally managed water removal system allowing the cellar wall to dry in an outward direction must be used to prevent moisture from the surrounding ground and storm water from penetrating the wall structure.
The heating plant emission rate of the micro combined heat and power system (microCHP) should be no greater than the emission rate of a regular boiler using the same fuel as the microCHP.
If air barriers or vapour barriers have been used in the structure, the seams, edges and penetrations must be tight.
If a lift or other device for moving between levels is installed in the exit of an existing building, the dwellings exit may be no less than 850 millimetres wide.
Cable routes should be provided from a metered electricity supply point to the future connection location.
The tread of steps in uncovered or unheated outdoor staircases must be no less than 390 millimetres, and the riser may be no more than 130 millimetres.

A space alongside the leading edge of a door should be provided to enable a wheelchair user to reach and grip the door handle, then open the door without releasing hold on the handle and without the footrest colliding with the return wall.
Moisture from the foundation wall and the base floors concrete slab must not transfer harmfully to the wooden sole plates or upper wall and floor structures.
Test data must be from a minimum of five in-situ measurements of the same module types and link details as used in the actual building.
Biomass heating supplemented by an alternative appliance (e.g. gas) - the CO2 emission factor and primary energy factor should be based on a weighted average for the two fuels.
Multiple cooling units should be provided with controls that ensure that the combined plant operates in its most efficient modes.
On-site electricity generation should be provided with automated controls that support the design of the system and the intended use.
Where sheathing board forms the air barrier, airsealing tape should be applied at junctions and edges.
The seasonal energy efficiency ratio of an air conditioner working in cooling mode should be a minimum of 4.0.
Only the proportion of openings which can be opened with a very low risk of occupants falling from height should be considered to form part of the overheating mitigation strategy.
Reasonable provision shall be made in the design and installation of electrical installations in order to protect persons operating, maintaining or altering the installations from fire or injury.
